known_facts_book1: The marvelous, uncivilized fairy country where Dorothy's cyclone-borne house comes down, cut off from the rest of the world by a great deadly desert on every side.
Divided into four countries by colour and compass: the blue Munchkin East, the yellow Winkie West, the red Quadling South, and the North, plus the green Emerald City at its centre.
Held only four witches in all: the Witches of the North and South are good, and the Witches of the East and West are wicked.
Cannot be left by the Winged Monkeys, who belong only to this land and may not cross the surrounding desert.

known_relations_book1.Emerald City: The green city at the centre of the land, ruled by Oz.
known_relations_book1.Dorothy: The Kansas girl set down in it by the cyclone.

not_in_this_book: the Land of Oz can be reached by road from Kansas

hallucination_signals: Oz turns out to be a dream Dorothy imagined
the Land of Oz is connected to Kansas by road

known_facts_book1: The great green city at the centre of the Land of Oz, ruled by the humbug Oz, and the travellers' goal along the road of yellow brick.
Everyone in it, and every visitor, must wear locked-on green spectacles, so that everything looks emerald green.
Is not really made of emeralds and is no greener than any other city: the Wizard admits he only put green spectacles on all the people to make the name fit.
Is guarded at its gate by the Guardian of the Gates, and holds the Wizard's Palace and Throne Room.
Is left in the rule of the Scarecrow after the Wizard departs by balloon.

known_relations_book1.Wizard: Its ruler, who deceives the people with green spectacles.
known_relations_book1.Scarecrow: Left to rule it when the Wizard leaves.

not_in_this_book: the Emerald City is truly built of solid emeralds
the Emerald City is the same as Kansas

hallucination_signals: the Emerald City is genuinely built of emeralds
the horse of a different color

known_facts_book1: Dorothy's home: the great gray prairie where she lives with Uncle Henry and Aunt Em on a small farm.
So sun-baked and gray that the grass, the house, and even Aunt Em have all turned the same dull gray.
The house has a single room with a trap-door leading to a cyclone cellar dug in the ground.
The place Dorothy longs to return to throughout the book and reaches again at the end by the power of the Silver Shoes.

known_relations_book1.Dorothy: Her gray prairie home, which she longs for through all her adventures.
known_relations_book1.Uncle Henry: The farmer she lives with there.

not_in_this_book: Kansas is in colour while Oz is gray
Dorothy's farm is destroyed by a tornado for good

hallucination_signals: the Kansas scenes are in sepia

known_facts_book1: The southern country of Oz, the land of the Quadlings, ruled by the Good Witch Glinda, the most powerful of all the witches.
A rich and happy country whose colour is red.
Reached only by passing the fighting trees, the Dainty China Country, and the hill of the Hammer-Heads.
Where Glinda's ruby-throned castle stands and where Dorothy learns how to get home.

known_relations_book1.Dorothy: Who journeys there to ask Glinda for help home.

not_in_this_book: the Land of the South is ruled by a Wicked Witch

hallucination_signals: the Wicked Witch of the South
the southern country is a wasteland

known_facts_book1: The Wizard's palace at the heart of the Emerald City, where visitors are lodged and prepared before being admitted to Oz.
Holds the Throne Room where Oz receives each visitor alone in a different terrible shape.
Behind the throne stands the screen from which the little old humbug works his illusions.
Provides the silk from which the Wizard builds his escape balloon.

known_relations_book1.Throne Room: The chamber within it where Oz grants audiences.
known_relations_book1.Emerald City: The city it stands at the centre of.

not_in_this_book: the Palace is stormed by an army in battle

known_facts_book1: The great domed hall in the Wizard's Palace where Oz receives visitors, one at a time.
There the Wizard appears to each traveller in a different form: a great Head, a lovely Lady, a terrible Beast, and a Ball of Fire.
There the humbug is finally exposed when Toto tips over the corner screen that hides the little old man.
The soldier says Oz sits there day after day and keeps a great pot of courage in it.

known_relations_book1.Wizard: Who holds audience there in shifting shapes.
known_relations_book1.Dorothy: Who is received there and to whom Oz appears as a great Head.
